A.explanation: Inverts the slit spacing to $3 \times 10^5$ per metre and multiplies by $G$, which gives $1/\lambda$ behaviour not $\lambda$.

B.explanation: Uses the correct spacing $3.3 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$ but multiplies by $G$ instead of dividing, confusing gradient $G = d/\lambda$ with $\lambda/d$.

C.explanation: From $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, $n = (d/\lambda)\sin\theta$ so $G = d/\lambda$ and $\lambda = d/G$ with $d = 3.3 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: Divides raw $300$ lines per mm by $G$ without converting lines per mm to spacing in metres, so units are not metres.

hints: Notice the axes: $n$ is plotted vertically against $\sin\theta$ horizontally, so gradient $G = n/\sin\theta$.
Recall the grating equation $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ and rearrange it to the form $n = (...)\sin\theta$ to identify what $G$ equals.
Calculate the grating spacing $d$ in metres from $300$ lines per mm using $d = 1/300 \text{ mm}$, then solve $G = d/\lambda$ for $\lambda$.
walkthrough: Start with the diffraction grating equation for order $n$: $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, where $d$ is the distance between adjacent slits.
Rearrange for the plotted y-variable $n$: $n = \left(\frac{d}{\lambda}\right)\sin\theta$. This is $y = mx$ form with $x = \sin\theta$.
Therefore the gradient of the $n$ against $\sin\theta$ graph is $G = \frac{d}{\lambda}$, so $\lambda = \frac{d}{G}$.
Find $d$ in metres: $d = \frac{1}{300} \text{ mm} = \frac{1 \times 10^{-3}}{300} \text{ m} \approx 3.3 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.
Substitute $d$ into the expression for wavelength: $\lambda = \frac{3.3 \times 10^{-6}}{G}$ metres. This is option C.
